name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,803

entries.clue: With bows bent, finally ready for battle (3,5)

blocks.note: W is the standard abbreviation for with
a bow is a curve, an arch

annotation.surface: An archer's instruction: string the bows, you are ready to fight.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is slang for cash, so ready for battle is money set aside to fight with. 'Bows bent' reads as one image, but 'bent' is only there for its last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A war chest is a fund of ready money reserved for a campaign or fight.

entries.clue: Finally working on size 15 shoes? (2,4,4)

blocks.note: plain adverb: in the end, after a long wait
a last is the foot-shaped block a cobbler builds a shoe on; enormous shoes need a long one, and 'at' is working on

annotation.surface: Someone at last getting round to making enormous shoes.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half is cryptic: a cobbler making very big shoes would be working at a long last. The question mark flags the pun.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain idiom for finally that stresses how long the wait was; the second reading is a cobbler busy on an outsized last.

entries.clue: Queen roughly treated in tower, Henry heard (9,6)

indicatorNotes.treated: the letters are processed, worked over into a new order

blocks.note: IN TOWER + H (henry, the unit) + HEARD, rearranged

annotation.surface: A queen manhandled in the Tower while Henry listened.
annotation.walkthrough: Catherine Howard, Henry VIII's fifth wife, was held in the Tower before her execution, so the surface is history. 'Henry' is not the king here but H, the symbol for the henry, a unit of inductance.
annotation.definitionFit: Catherine Howard was Queen of England as Henry VIII's fifth wife.

entries.clue: Pass German egg sandwiches that might make him sick (1,4)

indicatorNotes.sandwiches: the egg holds the pass between its halves, like bread round a filling

blocks.note: a col is a mountain pass

annotation.surface: Handing someone egg sandwiches that turn out to make him ill.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface hides its own answer: egg sandwiches are a classic source of food poisoning. 'Pass' looks like a verb (hand over) but is the noun, a col.
annotation.definitionFit: E. coli is a bacterium that can cause food poisoning, so it might make someone sick.

entries.clue: Fighter jet's broken flap (7)

blocks.note: a flap is a fuss, an ado

annotation.surface: A fighter jet with a damaged wing flap.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flap' reads as part of an aircraft wing; it is the informal flap meaning a panic or fuss.
annotation.definitionFit: The Panavia Tornado is a combat jet flown by the RAF and others.

entries.clue: Intimate shot of poor quality (6)

blocks.note: an intimate is a close friend, a pal
have a shot = have a try

annotation.surface: A close-up photograph that came out badly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Intimate shot' reads as a photograph; 'Intimate' is a noun here, a close friend.
annotation.definitionFit: Paltry means meagre or worthless, of poor quality.

entries.clue: Drug dealer keeps one pound back, for bookmaker? (9)

indicatorNotes.keeps: the dealer holds the other letters inside

annotation.surface: A drug dealer holding back a pound, perhaps to pay a betting shop.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bookmaker' suggests a betting shop, as British bookies are; taken literally it is a maker of books, and the question mark admits the pun.
annotation.definitionFit: A publisher is, literally, someone who makes books.

entries.clue: Large income, more expensive wine, extra tuition (8,7)

blocks.note: L = large, as on clothing labels
prices that are up are higher

annotation.surface: A list of luxuries: big salary, pricier wine, private tutoring.
annotation.walkthrough: The break falls in the wrong place: EARNINGS takes the S that begins SUPPORT, so the pieces do not line up with the two words of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Learning support is extra teaching given to pupils who need help.

entries.clue: Pole back in Katowice travelled on (4)

indicatorNotes.back in: the back of Katowice is its final letter

annotation.surface: A Pole returning home to Katowice, a Polish city, and travelling on.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pole' is capitalised to look like a Polish person, and Katowice supports that; it is a rod. 'Back' could suggest reversal, but it takes only the end letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Rode means travelled on, as on a horse or bus.

entries.clue: British house plastered (6)

blocks.note: house (housey-housey) is the old name for bingo, a lotto game

annotation.surface: A British house covered in plaster.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plastered' reads as a building finish; it is slang for very drunk. House, or housey-housey, is a British name for bingo, a form of lotto.
annotation.definitionFit: Blotto and plastered are both slang for very drunk.

entries.clue: Health food stocked by Liverpool markets in a fresh way (8)

indicatorNotes.stocked by: the food is held in stock inside the other word

blocks.note: the Reds is Liverpool Football Club's nickname

annotation.surface: Liverpool's street markets selling health food to look modern.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Markets' looks like a noun, places selling food; it is the verb, and the definition is the whole phrase.
annotation.definitionFit: To rebrand is to market something under a new image.

entries.clue: Getting pregnant achievable by half of people? (12)

annotation.definition: Getting pregnant achievable by half of people?

blocks.note: the surface reading: conception, and the act that brings it about
only males can do the necessary, half of people; the word also splits as IN + SEMI (half) + NATION (people)

annotation.surface: A remark on who can make someone pregnant.
annotation.walkthrough: Read the answer as IN SEMI-NATION: half of a people is a semi-nation. The question mark flags that pun on top of the plain meaning.
annotation.definitionFit: Insemination is the introduction of semen that leads to getting pregnant.

entries.clue: Talented child beginning to work less than class (10)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: take the first letter of work

blocks.note: a class is a kind, a sort

annotation.surface: A gifted pupil who, starting work, falls behind the class.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface places 'class' in a school, but it means a category.
annotation.definitionFit: A wunderkind, German for wonder-child, is a prodigy.

entries.clue: Skimpy costume Colin modelled with reluctance (9)

indicatorNotes.modelled: the letters are shaped into a new form

annotation.surface: Colin reluctantly modelling a very revealing outfit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Modelled' sits naturally with 'costume' as a catwalk verb. Strictly LOTH is the adjective reluctant, so 'with reluctance' has to be read loosely.
annotation.definitionFit: A loincloth is a single strip of cloth round the hips, about as skimpy as costumes get.

entries.clue: Conventional scout bizarrely worshipped mother (9)

indicatorNotes.bizarrely: the letters of scout are put in a strange order

blocks.note: Mary, mother of Jesus, venerated by Christians

annotation.surface: A normally conventional scout oddly worshipping his mother.
annotation.walkthrough: The joke is the contradiction: a 'conventional' scout behaving bizarrely.
annotation.definitionFit: Customary means usual, in line with convention.

entries.clue: Common sense feature of Moscow Olympics? (4)

blocks.note: practical wit, from the Greek word for mind
the United States boycotted the 1980 Moscow Games, so its absence was the feature; read the answer as two words

annotation.surface: A quiz question about what the Moscow Olympics lacked.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half is cryptic: the American-led boycott meant the 1980 Moscow Games had no US team, which is the answer split as NO US.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the Greek word for mind, used in British English for practical good sense.

entries.clue: Somewhat misleading description of Lewis, say (4)

indicatorNotes.Somewhat: only some of the word is used

blocks.note: the letters sit in positions two to five of the word

annotation.surface: A remark that calling Lewis something is a little misleading.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is true: Lewis is not an island on its own but the northern part of Lewis and Harris in the Scottish Hebrides, so 'isle' is a somewhat misleading description.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Lewis is conventionally named as one, though it shares a single landmass with Harris.

entries.clue: Day a Murdoch journalist wrote for Private Eye, perhaps (9)

annotation.surface: A Murdoch reporter moonlighting at Private Eye, the satirical magazine.
annotation.walkthrough: Murdoch suggests Rupert the press owner, which suits 'journalist'; it is Iris Murdoch. Private Eye is a British satirical magazine that often mocks Rupert Murdoch.
annotation.definitionFit: Private Eye mocks public figures, so writing for it is satirising them.

entries.clue: Without work, top referee painting club, perhaps (7)

indicatorNotes.Without: top loses the letters for work

annotation.surface: An idle referee painting a picture of a football club.
annotation.walkthrough: OP, short for opus, is the crossword's usual 'work'. The definition is the three-leafed shape of the club suit in cards.
annotation.definitionFit: The club symbol in playing cards is a trefoil, a three-lobed leaf shape.

entries.clue: Broke English taboo, returning meals (2,4,6)

indicatorNotes.returning: the letters go back the way they came

annotation.surface: Someone who broke an English rule about eating.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Broke' looks like the verb (broke a taboo); it is the adjective, meaning penniless. The uppers of a shoe are what is left when the soles wear through.
annotation.definitionFit: On one's uppers means very poor, having worn one's shoes down to the uppers.

entries.clue: Defeat prearranged after leading (5)

annotation.surface: A match-fixing scandal: the result was arranged once one side was ahead.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leading' is the sporting sense, ahead in a match, which fits the match-fixing story the surface tells.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from sport: a shock win over the favourite, or the verb for inflicting one.

entries.clue: Silver in sport topping for Italian (4)

annotation.surface: An Italian topping the sport and taking silver.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Topping for Italian' reads as someone beating an Italian; it is a sauce on pasta.
annotation.definitionFit: Ragù is an Italian meat sauce served on pasta.

entries.clue: Eponymous tortoise beginning to gain, 400m back? (8)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: take the first letter of gain

blocks.note: a lap of a standard running track is 400 metres
back, as in years back, is ago

annotation.surface: A tortoise starting to catch up after falling a lap behind.
annotation.walkthrough: The Galápagos Islands are named after the galápago, Spanish for tortoise, hence eponymous. The surface nods to the tortoise and the hare.
annotation.definitionFit: Galápago is the Spanish tortoise that gave the Galápagos Islands their name.

entries.clue: Good person with awful smell not fussed (6)

annotation.surface: A decent person who stinks but does not care.
annotation.walkthrough: OLID is a rare word for stinking, worth knowing.
annotation.definitionFit: Stolid means impassive, showing no fuss or emotion.

entries.clue: Star in need of a drink makes several (6)

annotation.surface: A thirsty celebrity who then drinks several.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Star' reads as a celebrity; it is the Sun.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: assorted, several of various kinds, as in 'sundry expenses'.

entries.clue: Faulty elements limiting the Dualit range (8)

indicatorNotes.limiting: only the limits, the outer letters, of 'the' are used
indicatorNotes.Faulty elements: the component letters are faulty, out of order

blocks.note: Dualit, a British toaster brand, used as it stands

annotation.surface: A repair report: broken heating elements have cut a toaster brand's range.
annotation.walkthrough: Dualit is a British maker of toasters and kettles, which is why heating elements feature. The surface makes 'range' a product line; it means scope or freedom.
annotation.definitionFit: Latitude means range or scope, freedom to act.
